doc.title: Henry Johnson interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 30, 1995

title: Blues feeling in his playing from Memphis and Chicago
summary: Woods praises his clean, bluesy playing; Johnson credits growing up on blues and gospel in Memphis and Chicago.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: Let me ask you a few questions about your guitar playing. First of all, I caught your set with Joe Williams, and two things I noticed about your playing. First of all it was really fine playing. I was excited to hear guitar playing that good, that clean, that crisp. But also, that marvelous blues influence in your playing. And it didn’t matter what type of tune it was. There was that authenticity that only comes from a player who understands the blues.

Yeah, that’s definitely there. It comes from experience and then too, I was raised in Chicago, and I spent some time in Memphis. In fact when I first started playing I was living in Memphis, Tennessee, and as you know Memphis is the home of B.B. King and a lot of other people, so I came up listening to the blues and Gospel music. And in Chicago, a lot of the blues players migrated from the South to Chicago. So I was still getting the same thing. And all around Chicago any night of the week you can go hear blues. And I just always loved that, the blues first, and I felt that anything that you play should have some sort of feeling in it, no matter what kind of tune it is. So that always got instilled in me, and by Joe being the great blues singer that he is, it always comes out with him. He does the same thing. He can sing blues sophisticated, but it always has that tendency to make you believe what he’s saying.
